subject: [PATCH v5 0/5] sunrpc: hardcode pool_mode to pernode, remove other modes

reviews.author: NeilBrown
reviews.summary: Reviewer NeilBrown noted that hardcoding pool_mode to pernode may have costs, such as increased code size, and requested further consideration of these trade-offs.
reviews.raw_body:
In general, yes.  But it is not without cost.  Sometimes the cost
matters.
Interface size has an abstract value.  Code size can have concrete
value.  Comparing them is subjective I guess.
I have no concrete evidence that there is a problem, so I'll stop
objecting.

Thanks,
NeilBrown

2026-07-09.patch_summary: This patch series hardcodes the pool mode to per-node, removing other modes and addressing issues such as scheduling RPCs to pools with no threads. It also implements suggestions from Neil to eliminate the serv.sv_nrpools field, which has the side effect of reducing the modulus operations in the svc_pool_for_cpu() hotpath. The patches include fixes for comment cleanups, shortcoming of existing code, and auto-thread-placement case. The approach taken is to ensure that each populated node has at least one thread and prevent routing requests to empty pools.
